podcast.body: Released in 1978, this album by Roy Cooder is considered an early attempt at an all-digital rock album. It was recorded using a special 3M machine that captured digital signals to tape, however, digital mixing boards were not yet available, so the mixing and mastering processes were still analog. "At some point, to a 1978 album entitled Bop to You Drop by Roy Kuder, who used a special 3M machine that recorded digital signals to tape."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: Released in 1979, *Bop Till You Drop* by Ry Cooder is identified as seemingly the first album to be recorded entirely using digital technology. This release marked a significant milestone in the evolution of recording techniques, showcasing the early adoption of digital methods. "This seems to be the first old digital album when it comes to recording."
